column1: # English letter names and digit words as an Arabic speaker says them, fully pointed,
# for lang "ar". Columns: the character; the English word that names it; the pointed
# A letter's consonant skeleton is the spelling Arabic writing attests for that letter,
# each one cited to the page that prints it beside a Latin initialism in the table in
# docs/normalization.md. Its vowels are the English letter name's, so that two letters
# said differently in English are said differently here: G is "gee" and J is "jay" on
# one skeleton. tests/test_textnorm.py holds every letter to its cited spelling and to
# being heard apart from every other, B and P excepted.
# The digit words are nativized from data/donor_lexicons/en-GB.tsv, which is where every
# row came from before the letters were cited; tests/test_textnorm.py still holds them
# No part of this table has been checked by a human speaker of Arabic.
